newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi to announce results of mining tenders soon.
newsitem.headline: Saudi to announce results of mining tenders soon.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Oil Minister Ali bin Ibrahim al-Nuaimi said on Wednesday the results of four mining tenders offered in 1995 would be made public soon, but did not give details on the timeframe.
"The results of the mining tenders will be announced soon after the evaluation of offers is completed," he said during a university lecture.
"There are a lot of queries so sometimes we have to go back to source to reply to them.

"All (mining) projects are open to the private sector which can participate on its own, with international firms or with Maadin (the newly-established Saudi Arabian Mining Co)," he said after a lecture at Riyadh's King Saud University.
The minister said mining -- including gold mining -- in the kingdom had made impressive strides in recent years.
"The total number of mining licences granted to date is more than 700," he said, adding they covered substances such as gypsum, limestone, granite and marble.
Officials and experts say Saudi Arabia has abundant minerals and commercially-exploitable reserves of gold, zinc, copper, bauxite and phosphates.
